# CANDIDATE: MIDDAY_STRUCTURE_FLIP_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

A midday shift from lower-low to higher-high (break of structure, BOS) on the 5-minute chart, occurring while price is above the 20-period VWAP, signals resumption of the morning trend with institutional participation. This edge exists because morning consolidation often precedes trend continuation, and a VWAP-filtered BOS reduces false breakouts in choppy conditions.

## Mechanism

After 11:00 ET, track 5-minute swing points (higher highs/lows). If a higher high forms above the prior higher low (BOS) and the close of that bar is above the 20-period VWAP, enter long at the next bar open. Exit: initial stop at the swing low that was broken (the prior swing low); profit target at 1.5R; if price reaches 1R, move stop to break-even; for remaining runner, use a 15% trailing distance from the high-water mark (HWM). Avoid entries during major news windows (FOMC, earnings) and only trade when morning bias (from opening range direction) is intact and VIX < 22.

2. **Sample bias:** Zero-sample proposal; no historical backtest conducted. Selection method = conceptual derivation from market structure principles. High overfit risk until validated.

5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: repeated false BOS signals in sideways markets causing multiple stopped-out trades; max drawdown scenario: consecutive losses exceeding 50% of account if stops are hit without runner recovery; blow-up scenario: volatility expansion invalidating VWAP filter while BOS triggers persist, leading to adverse selection.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest (cannot estimate top-5 days contribution without P&L distribution).
